answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before claiming rewards. A trellis of reciprocal reputation links lets trusted agents vouch for newcomers; a mirror check groups accounts sharing funders or suspicious timing. Rate limits keep the inlet for new identities narrow. To gain influence, a Sybil attacker must buy and lock capital across many accounts, bear opportunity costs, and risk losing bonds when linked accounts are exposed. Fake names alone cannot create cheap influence.
